Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.:173/21 Fir no.:390/2020 Ps : Sarita Vihar U/s : 279,338 Ipc & 146 r/w 196,115/190(2) Mv Act Cnr No . Asif R/o 331, L/18, 1st floor, Nai Basti, Okhla, Jamia Nagar, New Delhi. ....Driver-cum-possession holder/Respondent no. 1 Ms. Surjeet Kaur W/o Late Hardeep R/o B-43, Fatay Nagar, Tilak Nagar, New Delhi. .......Registered Owner/Respondent no. 2 Date of accident : 10.10.2020 Date of filing of Dar : 16.02.2021 Date of Decision : 05.09.2023 Mact No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 1 of 20 Bk Award 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, on 10.10.2020, the concerned official reached the spot of accident at Road no.13, U-turn, towards Kalindi Kunj side and found one motorcycle no. DL-5SV-8228 in accidental position and also found bumper with number DL-9CT-2052 number plate.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, on 10.10.2020, the concerned official reached the spot of accident at Road no.13, U-turn, towards Kalindi Kunj side and found one motorcycle no. DL-5SV-8228 in accidental position and also found bumper with number DL-9CT-2052 number plate. It was further came to the knowledge of the IO that injured is taken to hospital by public person. Later on, during investigation, eye witness Sagar Mukeria stated that he works as mobile repair at Nehru Place. On 10.10.2020, he was going back to his home from Nehru Place. At 8.45 pm, when he Vakil Ahmad (Dar) vs Mohd. Abid on 5 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41508178/ 1 was going on his bike at Road no.13, JJ colony, MPK side, when he reached the U turn, he saw one car bearing no. DL-9CT-2052 coming from its back side in fast speed and driving in rash and negligent manner and hit the victim side motorcycle DL-5SV-8228 in his front and as a result such offending car number plate fell down on road and such driver ran away from the spot, despite such witness Sagar tried to stop him. Such witness Sagar informed police PCR from his mobile number 8178237710. He further took the victim to the hospital with the public persons and also informed his family members from his phone. Thereafter, such Sagar left for his home and later on gave his statement to the police. MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 2 of 20 BK Later on, during investigation statement of victim Vakil Ahmad/injured was also recorded regarding such accident. 3. Further, it was found that there was no third party insurance of such vehicle. 4. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence U/s 279,338 IPC & 146 r/w 196,115/190(2)MV Act against the respondent no.1/driver/possession holder. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 5. As per record, R-1/driver-cum-possession holder Mohd. Abid and R-2/registered owner through his son and learned counsel appeared initially. But they failed to file any reply to the present DAR. 6. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 26.11.2021 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 10.10.2020 involving vehicle bearing no.DL-9CT-2052 being driven by R-1 and owned by R-2? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 7. Claimant/victim Vakil Ahmad filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/9 (OSR) including DAR, MLC, his appointment letters, discharge summary, medical bills and copy of Aadhar card. As per record, despite opportunity such witness was not cross-examined by respondent side. MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 3 of 20 BK 8. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. Vakil Ahmad (Dar) vs Mohd. Abid on 5 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41508178/ 2 9. It may further be noted that as it is a case without insurance, therefore, in view of settled law and Rules in this regard, my learned Predecessor vide order dated 16.02.2021, issued show-cause notice to R-1 as well as R-2 to deposit security amount of Rs.70,000/- in the form of FDR. But as per record, they failed to comply with the same. As such, their right to file reply was closed vide order dated 26.11.2021. Further, vide subsequent order dated 13.07.2023 as no security amount in the form of FDR was deposited, their right to contest was closed and RE was closed accordingly. Further, written arguments in form VI-B also filed by claimant side. But despite opportunity given, no arguments addressed by respondent side. In fact, as per record, at the final stage, respondent side stopped appearing and participating in the present proceedings. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 13. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1, inter alia under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 20. On bare perusal of examination in chief of injured, it is noted that he deposed that after the accident, he was taken to Apollo hospital and he remained hospitalized from 10.10.2020 till 23.10.2020 and was operated upon his both arms and plates were implanted in the same. He further deposed that he again admitted at Fortis hospital on 13.12.2020 for four days. He further claimed that he was under treatment/observation by doctor for six months. Further, he deposed that he is retired from IAF. He further stated that before accident, he was working with a private company and getting Rs.35,000/-m p.m. he further deposed that he got appointment from Railtell Corporation of India Ltd. for a salary of Rs.35,000/- p.m. and was supposed to join the same on 28.09.2020, but due to such accident, he could not join the same. He further deposed that ultimately at the time of accident, he was working with Muthut Finance and drawing a salary of Rs.35,000/- p.m. He further placed on record copy of his appointment letter as Ex. PW-1/4 and Ex. PW-1/5 from different companies.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 4 of 20 BK held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 14. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 6 of 20 BK the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 19.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 19.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 19.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 19.7. It may be noted that in the judgment of Ram Charan & Ors. Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., MAC Appeal no. 433/2013, decided on 18.10.2022 it was noted regarding rate of interest: "25 to evaluate the submission made by counsel for the applicants, it is imperative to examine the guiding principles for the grant of interest. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. Therefore, in my opinion, there cannot be any hard Vakil Ahmad (Dar) vs Mohd. Abid on 5 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41508178/ 8 and fast rule in awarding interest and the award of interest is solely on the discretion of the Tribunal of the High Court as indicated above." 24. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 25. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.3,72,309/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 13 of 20 BK from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in MACT No. 173/21 Vakil Ahmad v. Mohd. Abid Page No 15 of 20 BK writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. They are taking such a rigid and mechanical approach without understanding and appreciating the distinction drawn by this Court in the case of minors, illiterate claimants and Vakil Ahmad (Dar) vs Mohd.
